phase6_authority: This file is the single authoritative Phase 5 handoff for Phase 6 Chapter 2 drafting within the approved MP1-R boundary.
authoritative_mp1r_scope: MP1-R: pressure-conditioned bending characterization of a defined TiNi wire bundle, with external-pressure structural characterization and optional SMA-spring/piston integration.

research_gap_register.exact_gap_wording: Defined reaction surfaces and candidate interfaces must be fixed before interpreting pressure-conditioned mechanics.
evidence_limiting: The issue is an unspecified project geometry, not a demonstrated literature deficit.
research_gap_register.generalizability: None as a gap; the fixed geometry defines the domain of any later result.
research_gap_register.testability: Directly testable as a design/control prerequisite.
research_gap_register.allowed_thesis_wording: Geometry and candidate reaction paths were explicitly defined before inference.
research_gap_register.prohibited_stronger_wording: The current geometry uncertainty is a new scientific gap.
research_gap_register.contribution_enabled: Enables valid interpretation of C1–C4; no standalone contribution.

research_gap_register.exact_gap_wording: Pressure-to-local-contact transmission bounds for the defined TiNi-bundle configuration are not established.
evidence_limiting: Related models assume or infer pressure/contact relations; no MP1-R local calibration is present.
research_gap_register.generalizability: Moderate if expressed as a transferable measurement/bounding procedure; numerical values remain configuration-bounded.
research_gap_register.testability: Yes, with independent pressure, geometry, resistance and local-N constraints.
research_gap_register.allowed_thesis_wording: Pressure-to-contact transmission is identified or bounded for the defined configuration.
research_gap_register.prohibited_stronger_wording: Pressure directly equals local normal force in general.

research_gap_register.exact_gap_wording: The contributions of sleeve compliance, packing, end motion and reaction-path motion to apparent stiffness are not separated for the defined system.
evidence_limiting: This is a confounder-control requirement for MP1-R, not a literature-wide knowledge gap.
research_gap_register.generalizability: Low-to-moderate; method may transfer, parameter values do not automatically transfer.
research_gap_register.testability: Yes, by geometry/deformation measurements and bounded alternative paths.
research_gap_register.allowed_thesis_wording: Alternative sleeve, packing and boundary contributions are bounded in the tested regime.
research_gap_register.prohibited_stronger_wording: Any residual after unmeasured boundary motion demonstrates H1.

research_gap_register.exact_gap_wording: The pressure-conditioned contribution of wire–wire versus wire–sleeve resistance is not identified from global response alone.
evidence_limiting: Interface-specific methods exist; their joint application to MP1-R is not demonstrated.
research_gap_register.generalizability: Moderate as an identification protocol; dominance result is configuration-specific.
research_gap_register.testability: Yes if independent interface constraints are feasible; otherwise report non-identifiability.
research_gap_register.allowed_thesis_wording: Interface contribution is identified or bounded under independent constraints.
research_gap_register.prohibited_stronger_wording: Interface disambiguation is already a demonstrated scientific knowledge gap or global bending proves dominance.

research_gap_register.exact_gap_wording: The association between global branches and local slip, rather than sleeve/end motion, is not established for MP1-R.
evidence_limiting: Related systems show branch/slip behavior, but MP1-R local slip is not directly measured.
research_gap_register.generalizability: Moderate for the branch-identification method; result is system-bounded.
research_gap_register.testability: Yes with local slip/strain and boundary-motion observations.
research_gap_register.allowed_thesis_wording: Global transitions are associated with local slip only where local evidence supports the association.
research_gap_register.prohibited_stronger_wording: A global branch or loop uniquely proves local slip.

evidence_limiting: Transformation-sensitive response is established in other domains; transfer to pressured bending is not direct.
research_gap_register.generalizability: Moderate across matched same-lot regimes, not universal across TiNi products.
research_gap_register.testability: Yes with same-lot constitutive, temperature and history measurements; phase-sensitive data if needed.
research_gap_register.allowed_thesis_wording: The work characterizes transformation activity in the accessed same-lot domain.
research_gap_register.prohibited_stronger_wording: TiNi identity proves transformation or transformation-dominated hysteresis.

evidence_limiting: Global loop work, DMA loss and F–δ measures are not interchangeable or independently partitioned.
research_gap_register.generalizability: Moderate as an attribution procedure; fractions remain regime-specific.
research_gap_register.testability: Partly; MP1-R may bound rather than fully partition contributions.
research_gap_register.allowed_thesis_wording: Contributions are partitioned or bounded within the tested regime.
research_gap_register.prohibited_stronger_wording: Aggregate hysteresis identifies the fraction caused by transformation or friction.

research_gap_register.generalizability: Potentially high only if a repeatable, transferable, held-out residual survives all controls; currently unproven.
research_gap_register.testability: Conditional and high burden; not required for thesis success.
research_gap_register.allowed_thesis_wording: An added term may be evaluated conditionally after conventional alternatives are bounded.

gap_adjudication_matrix.parent_question: What is the pressure-to-reaction-to-contact-force map in the proposed cross-section?
gap_adjudication_matrix.parent_disposition: Mixed: UQ01a is a project prerequisite; UQ01b/UQ01c are system-identification requirements.

subquestions.question: Which reaction surfaces and candidate wire–wire/wire–sleeve paths exist after geometry is fixed?
subquestions.rationale: The cross-section, reaction surfaces and interface candidates must be specified before a scientific claim can be posed. Their current absence is a scope/design condition, not evidence of a literature knowledge deficit.
subquestions.mp1_can_answer: Yes, by fixing and documenting the geometry; the result defines the system rather than closing a general scientific gap.
subquestions.allowed_wording: The study defines and controls the candidate reaction paths before interpreting pressure-conditioned response.
subquestions.prohibited_stronger_wording: The unspecified geometry represents a new scientific gap or proves a previously unknown mechanism.

subquestions.question: How does near-specimen pressure map to local N or defensible transmission bounds?
subquestions.rationale: Pressure, reaction load and local normal force are distinct. Existing models provide routes or assumptions, but the MP1-R path and local distribution are not identified without independent constraints.
subquestions.mp1_can_answer: Yes, as a bounded system-identification result using synchronized pressure, geometry, resistance and a local-N proxy or calibrated bounds. It need not recover a unique field everywhere.
minimum_observations: local-normal-force proxy or calibrated transmission bounds
subquestions.allowed_wording: The study identifies or bounds the pressure-to-contact transmission for the defined configuration.
subquestions.prohibited_stronger_wording: Fluid pressure equals inter-wire or wire–sleeve normal force universally.

subquestions.question: How much do sleeve compliance, packing, end and reaction motion contribute to apparent stiffness?
subquestions.rationale: These alternative load paths can change the measured bending response and must be separated from pressure-conditioned contact. Their contribution is system-specific and not a demonstrated general literature gap.
subquestions.mp1_can_answer: Yes, by measuring geometry/deformation and bounding end, sleeve and packing effects in the tested regime.
minimum_observations: end/reaction motion or a bound on it
subquestions.allowed_wording: The experiment bounds the contribution of sleeve, packing and boundary motion in the tested configuration.
subquestions.prohibited_stronger_wording: Any residual after an uncontrolled test proves a new pressure–material mechanism.

gap_adjudication_matrix.parent_question: Can interface contributions and local slip be identified from augmented observations?
gap_adjudication_matrix.parent_disposition: G4 system-identification requirements; Phase 3 explicitly prevents upgrading interface disambiguation into a literature gap.

subquestions.question: Which interface dominates pressure-conditioned resistance under independent interface constraints?
subquestions.rationale: Wire–wire and wire–sleeve resistance can both contribute. Existing dedicated tests are precedents, but global bending alone is confounded.
subquestions.mp1_can_answer: Yes, if independent interface constraints and resistance measurements are feasible; otherwise it must report bounded non-identifiability.
minimum_observations: separate wire–wire and wire–sleeve resistance tests or constraints
local slip/strain or equivalent interface proxy
global bending response and parasitic bounds
subquestions.allowed_wording: The study identifies the pressure-conditioned interface contribution within the tested geometry, or reports that dominance remains bounded but unresolved.
subquestions.prohibited_stronger_wording: The literature contains a demonstrated interface-discovery gap, or global bending alone proves wire–wire dominance.

subquestions.question: Do global branches correspond to local slip onset/progression rather than sleeve or end motion?
subquestions.rationale: Branch changes and hysteresis can arise from local slip, sleeve compliance, end motion or material state. The question concerns pathway attribution in the actual system.
subquestions.mp1_can_answer: Yes, with synchronized local relative-slip/strain observations and sleeve/end controls; otherwise retain branch labels as phenomenological.
minimum_observations: local relative slip or structural-wire strain
subquestions.allowed_wording: Observed global branches are associated with local slip only when independent local and boundary evidence supports that attribution.
subquestions.prohibited_stronger_wording: A force–deflection branch or loop by itself proves local slip.

gap_adjudication_matrix.parent_question: How should TiNi state and aggregate hysteresis be interpreted?
gap_adjudication_matrix.parent_disposition: G2 material-domain characterization plus G4 attribution; transformation is not assumed from the material name.

subquestions.question: Does structural TiNi transformation occur in the accessible bending domain?
subquestions.rationale: Transformation-sensitive TiNi response is established in other material domains, but activation in the same-lot strain/temperature/rate/history domain of this bending test is not established. This is a bounded material-domain characterization question, not a new mechanism claim.
subquestions.mp1_can_answer: Yes, by same-lot constitutive and temperature/history measurements matched to the accessed domain; a phase-sensitive measurement is useful if ordinary calibration cannot distinguish alternatives.
subquestions.allowed_wording: The study characterizes whether transformation is active in the accessed same-lot domain.
subquestions.prohibited_stronger_wording: TiNi identity proves active transformation or transformation-dominated hysteresis.

subquestions.question: Can transformation, friction and sleeve losses be partitioned beyond aggregate loop work?
subquestions.rationale: Aggregate loop work is not an identifiable partition. Separate material, interface and boundary observations are required; the question is attribution in one system rather than discovery of a new loss law.
subquestions.mp1_can_answer: Partly. MP1-R can produce bounded attribution or show that full partition is not identifiable with available observables.
minimum_observations: defined loop-work metric; phase-sensitive data if required
subquestions.allowed_wording: The study partitions or bounds the measured contributions within the tested regime.
subquestions.prohibited_stronger_wording: Aggregate hysteresis proves the fraction due to transformation or friction.

gap_adjudication_matrix.parent_question: What model capability and coupling claim are justified?
gap_adjudication_matrix.parent_disposition: G2 empirical model-adequacy characterization plus G9 for any additional-law claim.

subquestions.question: Can an appropriate locked conventional model predict reserved pressure–curvature paths and available local observables?
subquestions.rationale: Conventional contact, slip and transformation-aware formulations exist, but their predictive adequacy for the defined MP1-R configuration is not quantified. The missing result is model discrimination in a bounded system, not a new constitutive principle.
subquestions.mp1_can_answer: Yes, with locked parameters, predeclared metrics, calibration/validation separation and reserved pressure–curvature paths.
subquestions.allowed_wording: The study tests the predictive adequacy and validity limits of a conventional model for the defined configuration.
subquestions.prohibited_stronger_wording: The absence of an exact MP1-R equation proves conventional mechanics are insufficient.

subquestions.question: After alternatives are bounded, is an additional state-conditioned pressure/contact/material term identifiable and predictively necessary?
subquestions.rationale: The validated corpus does not justify claiming a broader scientific gap or a new law. This can become a conditional result only after H0a/H0b, confounders and reserved predictions are tested.
subquestions.mp1_can_answer: Only conditionally. MP1-R can support a residual/additional-term claim if it is repeatable, identifiable, transferable beyond a fit and required by held-out prediction; otherwise report no need for a new term.
subquestions.allowed_wording: An additional term is considered only if conventional alternatives fail predictively under bounded conditions.
subquestions.prohibited_stronger_wording: A new constitutive coupling law is required because the literature lacks the exact equation.

gap_adjudication_matrix.parent_question: Can Bench B reproduce the controlled-pressure structural envelope when integrated?
gap_adjudication_matrix.parent_disposition: G6 actuator validation plus G7 integration validation; not automatically scientific novelty.

subquestions.question: Can the SMA spring/piston reach and recover the connected-load pressure–volume envelope?
subquestions.rationale: This is a capability and operating-envelope question for the proposed source. SMA-to-fluid precedents exist; a different arrangement does not create scientific novelty by itself.
subquestions.mp1_can_answer: Yes, by measuring stroke, force, temperature, source/near-specimen pressure and recovery under known load/compliance.
subquestions.allowed_wording: The study characterizes the reachable and recoverable pressure–volume envelope of the proposed source.
subquestions.prohibited_stronger_wording: The spring/piston arrangement is a new SMA-fluid mechanism solely because its geometry differs.

subquestions.question: At matched pressure, temperature, loading and history, does integrated response agree with externally pressurized response?
subquestions.rationale: Agreement or mismatch between Bench A and Bench B tests whether separately characterized components integrate consistently. It is an integration-validation result unless a generalizable mechanism is established.
subquestions.mp1_can_answer: Yes, with matched specimen pressure, temperature, loading, history and synchronized response metrics.
subquestions.allowed_wording: The integrated source is validated against the externally controlled structural envelope within stated conditions.
subquestions.prohibited_stronger_wording: Unmatched integrated differences prove H1 or a new coupling.

primary_contribution: Quantitative pressure-conditioned bending characterization of the defined TiNi-bundle configuration, with a locked conventional model-discrimination baseline.
secondary_contributions: Interface/local-slip system identification when independent constraints are available.
Predictive discrimination of existing conventional mechanics on reserved paths.
conditional_stretched_contributions: An additional pressure/contact/material term only if independently identifiable and predictively necessary; not required for thesis success.

contribution_boundary_register.title: Quantitative pressure-conditioned bending characterization of the defined TiNi bundle.
required_evidence: repeatable near-specimen pressure and M–κ/declared stiffness maps
uncertainty-resolved pressure-conditioned effects or bounded null result
contribution_boundary_register.hypothesis_dependence: Does not require H1; valid under H0a or H0b.
contribution_boundary_register.generalizability: Defined material/geometry/regime, with transferable measurement boundary conditions rather than universal coefficients.
contribution_boundary_register.thesis_wording: A quantitative characterization of pressure-conditioned bending response and its repeatability in the defined TiNi-bundle configuration.
contribution_boundary_register.forbidden_wording: A universal pressure–stiffness law or first pressure-friction mechanism.
contribution_boundary_register.failure_safe_interpretation: If pressure has no repeatable effect, report the measured null/limit and the conditions under which modulation was not observed.

contribution_boundary_register.title: Discrimination of a locked conventional model against reserved MP1-R response.
required_evidence: uncertainty-aware prediction error and residual analysis
contribution_boundary_register.hypothesis_dependence: H0b may be supported; H1 is not required.
contribution_boundary_register.generalizability: Validity-boundary evidence for the tested class and regime; no universal model rejection.
contribution_boundary_register.thesis_wording: A controlled test of whether an existing conventional model predicts the defined response within stated bounds.
contribution_boundary_register.forbidden_wording: Conventional models are insufficient because one fit or simplification fails.
contribution_boundary_register.failure_safe_interpretation: If H0b predicts well, the result is a positive model-adequacy/validity-boundary finding.

contribution_boundary_register.title: Interface and local-slip system identification under independent constraints.
required_evidence: wire–wire and wire–sleeve constraints or tests
pressure/contact bounds independent of the resistance fit
contribution_boundary_register.hypothesis_dependence: Supports interpretation of H0b/H1 but does not require H1.
contribution_boundary_register.generalizability: Method-level transfer is possible; dominance results remain configuration-specific.
contribution_boundary_register.thesis_wording: The study identifies or bounds pressure-conditioned interface contributions in the defined bundle.
contribution_boundary_register.forbidden_wording: Global bending alone identifies interface dominance or discovers a new friction mechanism.
contribution_boundary_register.failure_safe_interpretation: If interfaces cannot be separated, report non-identifiability and retain the broader C1/C3 contribution.

contribution_boundary_register.title: Validated measurement/decomposition method for separating source, pressure-path, interface and material effects.
required_evidence: demonstrated improvement in claim identifiability over global bending alone
contribution_boundary_register.hypothesis_dependence: Independent of H1; it can support H0b or a bounded null.
contribution_boundary_register.generalizability: Potentially methodological if the protocol is explicitly validated and transferable.
contribution_boundary_register.thesis_wording: A validated decomposition protocol that enables bounded attribution in this class of pressure-conditioned bundles.
contribution_boundary_register.forbidden_wording: Building two benches is inherently novel or proves causality without matched controls.
contribution_boundary_register.failure_safe_interpretation: If decomposition is not validated, treat the benches as controls/objectives only.

contribution_boundary_register.title: Operating-envelope characterization of the SMA-spring-driven piston source.
contribution_boundary_register.hypothesis_dependence: Independent of H1; supports Bench B feasibility.
contribution_boundary_register.thesis_wording: Characterization of the source pressure–volume and recovery envelope.
contribution_boundary_register.forbidden_wording: A first SMA-fluid mechanism solely from the actuator arrangement.
contribution_boundary_register.failure_safe_interpretation: If the source misses the envelope, retain Bench A structural characterization and report integration infeasibility.

contribution_boundary_register.title: Matched validation of integrated SMA/piston and externally pressurized structural response.
required_evidence: matched p, temperature, load, history and geometry
common response metric and uncertainty comparison
contribution_boundary_register.hypothesis_dependence: Independent of H1; agreement can support H0b.
contribution_boundary_register.thesis_wording: The integrated source is validated against the external-pressure structural envelope under stated conditions.
contribution_boundary_register.forbidden_wording: Integration mismatch at unmatched conditions proves coupled physics.
contribution_boundary_register.failure_safe_interpretation: If integration fails, report source/transport limits without converting them into a material mechanism.

contribution_boundary_register.title: Additional state-conditioned pressure/contact/material law, only if independently necessary.
required_evidence: predictive improvement beyond refit and transfer test
contribution_boundary_register.hypothesis_dependence: Requires evidence supporting H1; never a thesis prerequisite.
contribution_boundary_register.generalizability: Must extend beyond one geometry/fit to merit a theoretical claim; currently unestablished.
contribution_boundary_register.thesis_wording: A candidate additional term is proposed only if the controlled evidence shows it is identifiable and predictively necessary.
contribution_boundary_register.forbidden_wording: A new constitutive law is required in advance.
contribution_boundary_register.failure_safe_interpretation: If H0b suffices or the term is not identifiable, no theoretical-law contribution is claimed.

primary_research_question.question: For a fixed TiNi-bundle geometry, material lot and loading history, how does controlled near-specimen pressure change the bending response, and how accurately does a locked conventional contact/friction/transformation-aware model predict reserved pressure–curvature paths?

secondary_research_questions.question: Which pressure-conditioned resistance pathway—wire–wire, wire–sleeve, or sleeve/end motion—can be identified or bounded using independent interface and local-slip observations?
Does the same-lot TiNi undergo transformation in the accessed strain/temperature/history domain, and what material-state control is required to interpret the measured response?

h0a_h0b_h1_role.definition: TiNi thermomechanical/material behavior sufficiently explains most observed response.
h0a_h0b_h1_role.role: Live explanatory alternative and material-control branch, not a required result.
support_evidence: same-lot transformation-sensitive response in accessed domain
pressure contrasts with sleeve/end effects bounded
material baseline predicts relevant response features

h0a_h0b_h1_role.thesis_success_dependency: NO; a negative or weak H0a result still supports C1/C3.

h0a_h0b_h1_role.definition: Existing contact/friction/stick–slip and transformation-aware material/boundary models suffice without a new constitutive coupling law.
h0a_h0b_h1_role.role: Primary baseline comparator; it must be tested before any added-law claim.
support_evidence: locked conventional model predicts reserved paths within predeclared bounds
independent interface and boundary observations are consistent
no repeatable residual requiring added coupling

independent observations show omitted state dependence

required_observations: all core observations plus OBS07–OBS10 and, if needed, OBS13

success_null_kill_conditions.success_condition: Repeatable pressure-conditioned M–κ/declared stiffness branches are resolved beyond measurement and history uncertainty for the defined geometry and regime.
success_null_kill_conditions.null_baseline_success: A small or absent pressure effect, when uncertainty-resolved, is a valid bounded characterization and can still support C3 by defining a null regime.
success_null_kill_conditions.kill_condition: Pressure/specimen state cannot be measured or controlled, geometry remains ambiguous, or repeatability is below the declared uncertainty so no quantitative response map is defensible.

success_null_kill_conditions.success_condition: A locked conventional model either predicts reserved paths within predeclared bounds or fails with a repeatable, uncertainty-resolved residual after confounders are bounded.
success_null_kill_conditions.null_baseline_success: H0b predicts well; model adequacy and validity boundary are positive results, and no new law is claimed.
success_null_kill_conditions.kill_condition: No parameter lock, no reserved paths, or no independent observations sufficient to distinguish fit quality from leakage/confounding.

success_null_kill_conditions.success_condition: Independent interface/local-slip observations identify a dominant contribution or produce defensible bounds on competing pathways.
success_null_kill_conditions.null_baseline_success: No dominance can be identified; report non-identifiability while retaining C1/C3.
success_null_kill_conditions.kill_condition: Only global bending is measured, or interface tests cannot be made independent of the same unknowns.

success_null_kill_conditions.success_condition: The source reaches and recovers a characterized connected-load pressure–volume envelope with repeatable timing and force/temperature records.
success_null_kill_conditions.null_baseline_success: The envelope is insufficient; Bench A can remain the structural study and the source limitation is reported as engineering validation failure.
success_null_kill_conditions.kill_condition: No reliable pressure/stroke/force record or no connected-load characterization.

success_null_kill_conditions.success_condition: Integrated and external responses agree within declared uncertainty under matched p, temperature, load, history and geometry, or the mismatch is traced to a bounded source/path effect.
success_null_kill_conditions.null_baseline_success: No integration claim is required if the source cannot reproduce the envelope; C1/C3 remain possible.
success_null_kill_conditions.kill_condition: Conditions cannot be matched or the source/structural clocks cannot be synchronized.

success_null_kill_conditions.success_condition: Only after H0a/H0b controls, a repeatable held-out residual requires an identifiable additional term that improves prediction beyond refitting.
success_null_kill_conditions.null_baseline_success: H0b suffices or the term is not identifiable; no new-law contribution is made.
success_null_kill_conditions.kill_condition: Residual disappears with controls, is fit-only, or cannot be separated from parameter/boundary uncertainty.

evidence_strength_restrictions: Use RP001–RP010 and E01–E05 only within their stated architecture/material/metric boundaries.
Treat RP011–RP016 as supported connections/analogue-only where marked.
Treat RP017–RP020 as unresolved; do not use them as established mechanisms.
S15 remains contextual review support; S18 identity/restrictions remain corrected; S19/S20/S21 have no scientific support role.

scientific_novelty.boundary: No generalizable new pressure–contact–material law or mechanism is currently established. A scientific novelty claim is conditional on a repeatable, transferable, held-out result beyond H0a/H0b.

system_novelty.boundary: The SMA-spring/piston, fluid path and TiNi structure may form a new implementation combination, but combination alone is not scientific novelty.

empirical_novelty.boundary: New quantitative characterization of pressure-conditioned bending in the defined TiNi-bundle regime may be claimed without a universal or first-ever statement.

methodological_novelty.boundary: A validated decomposition/identification protocol may be a methodological contribution if it demonstrably enables claims unavailable from global bending alone.

engineering_novelty.boundary: Source operating envelope, packaging and integration performance may be engineering contributions and must be labelled accordingly.

allowed_claims.wording: Validated related architectures show architecture-scoped pressure/confinement effects on bending response.
allowed_claims.boundary: No universal pressure–stiffness law or MP1-R transfer.

allowed_claims.wording: Conventional contact/slip and transformation-aware formulations exist and can serve as locked comparators.
The pressure-to-local-contact map, interface dominance, TiNi-state activation in the accessed domain and matched source integration are not established for MP1-R.
allowed_claims.boundary: These are unresolved/project-specific questions, not automatically literature gaps.

allowed_claims.wording: Bench A/B separation is a design rationale for attribution.
allowed_claims.boundary: It is not evidence that two benches are uniquely novel or mandatory.

conditional_claims.claim: A particular interface dominates or contributes a bounded fraction.
conditional_claims.required_result: Independent interface constraints and local/boundary observations.

conditional_claims.claim: TiNi transformation is active in the accessed domain.
conditional_claims.required_result: Same-lot matched constitutive/temperature/history or phase-sensitive evidence.

conditional_claims.claim: A conventional model predicts or fails on MP1-R.
conditional_claims.required_result: Locked parameters, reserved paths, declared metrics and uncertainty-aware comparison.

conditional_claims.claim: An additional coupling term is necessary.
conditional_claims.required_result: H0a/H0b and confounders bounded, repeatable held-out residual, identifiable predictive improvement.

conditional_claims.claim: Integrated SMA/piston response reproduces or fails to reproduce external-pressure response.
conditional_claims.required_result: Matched pressure, temperature, load, history, geometry and synchronized response.

prohibited_claims: First positive-pressure variable-stiffness structure or first positive-pressure fiber-jamming principle/model.
First SMA/friction mechanism or first SMA-controlled friction modulation of wire-based structures.
First NiTi wire-jamming system or first wire/fiber jamming system.
Fluid pressure directly equals every inter-wire or wire–sleeve normal force.
Global bending proves wire–wire jamming or identifies interface dominance.
NiTi transformation necessarily dominates MP1-R hysteresis.
NiTi identity alone proves active transformation in the accessible bending domain.
Conventional models are insufficient, definitively falsified, or rejected because one simplification fails.
A new constitutive pressure–contact–material coupling law is required.
Interface disambiguation is already a demonstrated literature-wide scientific knowledge gap.
No relevant prior work combines any of the MP1-R mechanisms.
S18 proves positive-pressure fiber jamming or is a direct S03 precursor.
S19, S20 or S21 supplies scientific mechanics evidence; S20's retired identity may not be restored.
SMA spring-to-fluid displacement is novel solely because the drive or geometry differs.
Universal SMA cooling/response time inferred from S04.
Integrated response differences at unmatched pressure, temperature or history prove H1.
Different geometry, material, pressure levels, more FEA/measurements or held-out testing alone establish novelty.
A global loop, DMA loss tangent or F–δ slope directly equals M–κ bending work or local friction loss.
A source pressure gauge alone establishes specimen pressure or contact force.
No previous research has studied this mechanism.
The unresolved pressure/contact map is itself a demonstrated scientific knowledge gap.
The project contribution requires H1-R to be supported.
A null pressure effect or successful H0b result makes the thesis scientifically invalid.
The current working title can be used as causal evidence that pressure-controlled friction has already been demonstrated in MP1-R.

approved_chapter2_gap_wording.safe_strongest_wording: The validated literature establishes pressure-dependent response in related architectures, but does not establish the pressure-to-local-contact transmission for the defined TiNi-bundle configuration.
approved_chapter2_gap_wording.more_conservative_wording: The pressure-to-contact relation remains unestablished for this configuration and must be bounded experimentally.
approved_chapter2_gap_wording.prohibited_wording: No previous research has studied pressure-to-contact transmission.

approved_chapter2_gap_wording.safe_strongest_wording: Interface-specific resistance tests provide precedents, while pressure-conditioned wire–wire versus wire–sleeve contribution remains a system-identification question for MP1-R.
approved_chapter2_gap_wording.more_conservative_wording: The dominant interface cannot be inferred from global bending alone.
approved_chapter2_gap_wording.prohibited_wording: Interface disambiguation is a literature-wide scientific gap.

approved_chapter2_gap_wording.safe_strongest_wording: NiTi state-sensitive response is established in tested domains, but transformation activity in the accessed same-lot bending domain is not established.
approved_chapter2_gap_wording.more_conservative_wording: The study will characterize whether transformation is active in the measured domain.
approved_chapter2_gap_wording.prohibited_wording: TiNi necessarily transforms and dominates hysteresis.

approved_chapter2_gap_wording.safe_strongest_wording: Existing conventional formulations provide a comparator, but their predictive adequacy for the defined MP1-R configuration has not been quantitatively tested on reserved paths.
approved_chapter2_gap_wording.more_conservative_wording: A locked conventional baseline is required before any stronger coupling claim.
approved_chapter2_gap_wording.prohibited_wording: The literature lacks the exact equation, so a new law is required.

approved_chapter2_gap_wording.safe_strongest_wording: The proposed source operating envelope and matched integrated/external response remain to be validated for the selected architecture.
approved_chapter2_gap_wording.more_conservative_wording: Actuator and integration performance are supporting validation tasks.
approved_chapter2_gap_wording.prohibited_wording: A different spring/piston arrangement is automatically a new scientific mechanism.

chapter3_implication_boundary.intervention: Controlled near-specimen pressure applied to a fixed, mentor-confirmed cross-section; Bench B source operation is a separate intervention clock.
chapter3_implication_boundary.control: Geometry, packing, reaction/sleeve path, material lot, temperature, loading rate, history, source versus specimen pressure, and cycle order.
chapter3_implication_boundary.measurement: M–κ or predeclared stiffness metric, near-specimen pressure, temperature, histories, boundary motion, local/interface observations and source records as required by the claim.
chapter3_implication_boundary.comparison: Externally pressurized Bench A versus integrated SMA/piston Bench B only at matched p, temperature, load, history and geometry.
chapter3_implication_boundary.validation: Uncertainty-aware repeatability, calibration/validation separation, independent interface/material controls and explicit null handling.
chapter3_implication_boundary.held_out_test: Reserved pressure–curvature paths for the locked conventional model; no post-hoc threshold or term selection.

working_title_audit.current_title: Characterization of Bending Stiffness in TiNi Wire Bundles Using Pressure-Controlled Friction Generated by an SMA-Spring-Driven Piston
working_title_audit.finding: The current title presupposes pressure-controlled friction and gives the piston a causal role before pressure-to-interface mapping and integration are established.
working_title_audit.conservative_title: Pressure-Conditioned Bending Characterization of TiNi Wire Bundles with an SMA-Spring-Driven Pressure Source
working_title_audit.mechanism_focused_conditional_title: Interface-Resolved Pressure–Friction–Bending Response of TiNi Wire Bundles under SMA-Spring-Driven Pressurization
working_title_audit.conditional_title_use: Use only after interface dominance and pressure-to-contact evidence are independently established.
